title: [dogfood:P1] Export/import round-trip silently DESTROYS community edits — producer re-export overwrites an externally updated answer with no diff/merge, and consumer import can never see the update (silent data loss, no conflict signal)
notes: Repro 2026-09-25 (scratch producer :18801 / consumer :18802, bare community remote /tmp on local host). 1) Producer exports answers 2,3,4 via POST /api/v1/export -> commit a950ae0, spec 8.1 layout OK. 2) A community editor clones, appends '**Update v2:** ...' to the solution body of go-string-reverse, pushes commit 6720124. 3) Consumer import (conflict_strategy replace) reports {added:0,updated:0,skipped:3} — the update is INVISIBLE (root cause = DF-OFF-BY-ONE-23 parse cut). 4) Producer re-exports answer 4 -> commit 719cec8, and 'grep -c Update v2' in the community repo goes 1 -> 0: the community edit is clobbered with zero warnings — the handler forces Push:true (handlers.go:940) and the engine only skips answers whose own freshly-formatted bytes are identical (writeItem has no upstream-diff check). Promised behavior per README component map: 'Pull community answers with diff + conflict resolution'. title: [dogfood:P1] extractSection cuts a solution body at its first embedded '---' — any corpus answer containing a horizontal rule swallows everything a community editor appends, and import then reports 'skipped: identical content' (silent no-op where an update is expected)
notes:
internal/import/git.go:561-577 extractSection(content, '## Solution') returns everything up to the FIRST of 
---
, 
## , 
# — but formatSolutionMD (internal/export/git.go:432) writes the stored solution TEXT verbatim, and corpus answers commonly END with a '---' rule inside the body (e.g. producer answer id=2 ends '...coercion (e.g., `"toString"` as a key).

---'). Byte-proven 2026-09-25: appending 'Update v2' text below that rule yields a parsed solution of exactly the old 830 bytes (simulate-parse + sqlite length comparison), so importAnswer's content-diff sees no change and reports ActionSkipped 'identical content' — the community edit silently vanishes at parse time, before conflict logic could ever fire. title: Generated solution accumulates per-event slices with no bound — the 47 GB allocation is in the solved code, not the harness
reasoning: The runaway was not the daemon (live cgroup 0.26 GB after the test exited) — it was the generated packet-level simulator. In the sandbox for problem class go-bbr-pacing-congestion-bandwidth-delay-probe (problem.json, 11:02) the agent wrote bbr/bbr.go (425 lines), bbr/sim.go (309 lines) and two *_test.go files; sim.go appends once per simulated event and never trims: sim.go:189 `s.queueAt = append(s.queueAt, QueuePoint{...})` and sim.go:106 `s.lossPlan = append(s.lossPlan, lossInjection{...})`. A deep-buffer bottleneck with a scripted ACK trace generates an unbounded number of events, so memory scales with simulated packets. The agent itself added an iteration guard in the test (debug_test.go:30 `if count > 5000000`) — evidence it already knew the loop could run away. Host-capping this (DF-OFF-BY-ONE-30) stops the blast radius but does not fix a solver that produces unbounded simulations.
fix_direction: Bound the work the solver is allowed to produce, at both ends. Prompt side: require that solutions to simulation classes declare their bounds (max simulated events/packets/seconds) and aggregate incrementally instead of retaining a record per event; state a memory budget the generated tests must respect. Harness side: measure the peak RSS of each test run and treat a run that approaches the cap as a rejected answer (with the measured number recorded against the problem id), so a rejected problem produces a finding rather than a host incident. Acceptance: (a) an unbounded simulation fixture is REJECTED by the harness with its measured peak recorded; (b) a bounded version of the same problem is accepted and verified; (c) the prompt/contract change is asserted by a test so it cannot silently regress.

title: Feeder pumps 3 problems 4x/day with no host-aware gate, and solver resource use is unobservable
reasoning: off-by-one-problem-feeder is an enabled cron job (0 5,11,17,23 * * *) whose prompt is 'generate and submit 3 hard, diverse problems to the pre-solve lab at http://localhost:8766' — its last run was 2026-10-03 11:01, one minute before the memory spike; the daemon then dequeues on a 60s loop, so 12 new problems a day feed a solver that also has 2,469 answers of history. Nothing checks whether the HOST can take it, and there is no per-solve visibility: a solve that allocated 47 GB left no metric, no counter and no alert — the only reason it was noticed was a human seeing 'RAM almost full'. Recurrence is the default state, not an edge case: it happened twice in twenty minutes on 2026-10-03.
fix_direction: Two halves.   ./off-by-one --port 18799 -db <scratch>/a.db -load-threshold -1 --mem-fraction 0.001 -cron-interval 2s -pi-agent <path> -bwrap /usr/bin/bwrap
then submitted a problem and polled it the way a submitting agent (or the remote Muster consumer) would.

  submit 200 (23.6 ms): {"submission_id":"sub_4fcc15", "status":"queued", "position":1, "estimated_time":"30s"}
  GET /api/v1/queue/sub_4fcc15 at t=2s, 6s, 12s, 20s — byte-identical every time:

  estimated_time "30s" and the queue entry kept repeating "30s" + position 1 for the whole 15 s window
  while the gate skipped.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT, NOT A DESIGN CHOICE: the queue wire shape already has a deferral-sized hole
(stage is a free string, status has no "deferred" class) and the daemon already persists the reason
(metrics.HostSnapshot.Reason: "load" | "memory" | "load+memory", internal/cron/loop.go:482-497).

`-cron-interval 60s` and its /stats reports avg_solve_time 5m41s — so a submitter can be quoted an
ETA of minutes, wait that long plus up to a full cron interval, and never learn that the box was
gated the entire time. "Deferred by host pressure" and "stuck" are indistinguishable from every
per-submission surface.

 - status "deferred"/stage "gated" plus a `gate_reason` (+ the HostSnapshot the observer already
   holds) while the entry is the queue head and checkIdle keeps returning ErrNoIdle; and

   the cron interval added: interval 60s + avg solve 5m41s).

queue entry names the gate reason within one interval.

title: [P2] A solve killed by a configured limit reports a cause-blind reason (signal: killed / exit status 139) naming neither the limit, its value, nor the knob
reasoning:
DOGFOOD 2026-10-16 (run 18), legs B + arm 3 — a killed solve reports a CAUSE-BLIND reason.

REAL USE: an operator boxing the lab into a small VPS sets the documented memory/timeout knobs and
submits. Two arms, two different limits firing, two different — and equally useless — reason strings.

ARM 1 (the configured SOLVE TIMEOUT fires):
  flags: --solve-mem-mb 128 --solve-timeout 30s, OB1_BWRAP_TIMEOUT=60, gate disabled
  queue entry: status "failed", stage "failed",
      failure_reason "pi-agent exec: signal: killed (stdout=)"
  started_at 2026-10-16T11:46:37Z, completed_at 11:47:07Z  → 30.0 s wall, exactly the configured
  --solve-timeout; /metrics last_solve.peak_rss_bytes = 0.022 GiB, i.e. the 128 MiB cap was NEVER
  approached. The string does not name the timeout, and the only 30 s limit on the box was one the
  operator had set themselves.

ARM 2 (the configured MEMORY CAP fires):
  flags: --solve-mem-mb 32 --solve-timeout 300s, OB1_BWRAP_TIMEOUT=120
  queue entry: status "failed", failure_reason "pi-agent exec: exit status 139 (stdout=)"
  died in 67 ms, /metrics peak_rss_bytes 0.016 GiB. Exit 139 = SIGSEGV: a crash-shaped string. A
  submitter reads "the solver segfaulted", not "your per-solve cap is 32 MiB".

WHAT THE DAEMON KNEW AND DID NOT SAY: the startup line names the knobs —
"cron loop started: interval=2s loadThreshold=-1.0 solve-mem-mb=32 reject-rss=25 MiB"; /metrics
carries killed/peak_rss_bytes/alert_threshold_bytes; the log line adds the peak
("cron: solve failed for sub_68daad (peak_rss=0.016)"). None of it reaches the queue entry, whose
reason is the raw error from internal/solver/piagent.go:272 (`fmt.Errorf("pi-agent exec: %w
(stdout=%s)", err, ...)`). The docs push the disambiguation onto the operator: docs/api-reference.md
"Solve memory bounds" — "A repeated `signal: killed` at exactly the configured cap is the sandbox cap
doing its job; verify the configured value before treating it as a solver failure."

FAIL-CLOSED HELD (stated so the row is precise): nothing was committed in either arm — /api/v1/stats
total_answers 0 and total_problems 0 on both scratch nodes. The defect is attribution, not integrity.

FIX DIRECTION: classify the kill at the source and name the limit + its configured value in
failure_reason, e.g. "solve killed by --solve-mem-mb 32 (RLIMIT_AS) after 0.07 s: exit status 139"
vs "solve killed by --solve-timeout 30s". The three candidate causes (per-solve cap, solve timeout,
bwrap outer timeout) are all known to the daemon at kill time.

title: [P3] A normal gate skip logs as "cron: tick error: cron: system is not idle" on every tick — the steady state of a busy box reads as a permanent error
reasoning:
DOGFOOD 2026-10-16 (run 18), leg A — a normal gate decision is logged as an error, every tick.

EVIDENCE (scratch node :18799, --mem-fraction 0.001 -cron-interval 2s, gate tripped by design):
  $ grep -iE 'cron' serve.log | tail -8
  2026/10/16 06:45:57 cron: tick error: cron: system is not idle
  2026/10/16 06:45:59 cron: tick error: cron: system is not idle
  ... 10 identical lines in 20 s (one per tick).

The same line is what the LIVE unit emits whenever this host is busy (it runs -cron-interval 60s), so
a busy box produces a permanent stream of "tick error" lines — including on a deployment whose whole
point is to wait for idle cycles.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT: ErrNoIdle is a DECISION (internal/cron/loop.go:497 returns it from checkIdle), but
Run logs every non-canceled tick error with the same prefix (internal/cron/loop.go:378-380
`l.cfg.Logger.Printf("cron: tick error: %v", err)`). An operator (or the fleet's own log scanners)
keying on "tick error" gets a false alarm at cron cadence exactly when the gate is working correctly,
and the same prefix covers real failures (reap errors, dequeue errors, solve failures) with no way to
tell them apart in aggregate.

FIX DIRECTION: log gate skips on their own path — e.g. `cron: deferred — host busy (memory): used
0.368 / threshold 0.001` (the reason string and the HostSnapshot already exist at that point) — and
keep "tick error" for genuine errors. Acceptance: with the gate tripped, N ticks produce N deferral
lines and zero "tick error" lines.

title: [P2] Export pushes are not atomic: when the push fails after the local commit, the stranded commit is silently skipped forever — later exports 200 with commit_sha empty and files_changed>0 while NOTHING reaches the target
reasoning:
{
  "id": "DF-OFF-BY-ONE-50",
  "title": "[P2] Export pushes are not atomic: when the push fails after the local commit, the stranded commit is silently skipped forever — later exports 200 with commit_sha "" and files_changed>0 while NOTHING reaches the target",
  "status": "pending",
  "priority": "P2",
  "complexity": 3,
  "depends_on": [],
  "blocks": [],
  "created_by": "off-by-one-dogfood",
  "created_at": "2026-10-16T07:20:00Z",
  "reasoning": "DOGFOOD 2026-10-16 (run 18), REVIEW-OB-014 delta re-proof pass — a NEW defect surfaced by the round trip, discriminating probes included.

REPRO (scratch nodes on HEAD code, REST surface only, git-daemon fixture):
  1. POST /api/v1/export {answer_ids:[1,2,3], target_repo: git://127.0.0.1:18923/fixture2.git}
     with the daemon NOT exporting receive-pack -> HTTP 500 export_failed "git push: ... access
     denied or repository not exported" (correct failure surfaced), BUT the export clone
     (/tmp/ob-df-1016/w1b) now holds a LOCAL COMMIT (4d87d7e "stranded repro") — files committed,
     push failed. The target has nothing.
  2. Make the daemon push-able. Re-export THE SAME answer_ids -> HTTP 200 with
     {"commit_sha":"", "files_changed":9} — engine stageAndCommit diffs cached files, finds
     nothing new (the files are already committed locally), and EARLY-RETURNS before any push
     (internal/export/git.go stageAndCommit: `if strings.TrimSpace(out) == "" { return nil }`).
     The stranded commit stays local FOREVER: fixture commits after step 2 = '' (empty).
  3. Third export with a DIFFERENT id -> 200 {commit_sha:71e35e3}; upstream log now shows BOTH
     71e35e3 AND the stranded 4d87d7e riding along.

USER IMPACT: an exporter whose push failed once (network blip, auth, read-only target) gets
NO recovery path from the API: the natural retry (same request) silently answers success and
uploads nothing, with a contract-ambiguous response (commit_sha empty + files_changed 9).
Ambiguity is load-bearing here: docs/api-reference.md documents 200 as `{"commit_sha":
"abc123...", "files_changed": 2}` and never says commit_sha may be empty on a 200.
This also reproduces the confusing first leg of the round trip (round1 evidence:
200 {commit_sha:'', files_changed:9} right after a failed push round) — i.e. the state after
ANY failed push, not a race.

NOTE (interacting contract, same engine): re-exporting the same ids after a SUCCESSFUL push also
answers 200 {commit_sha:"", files_changed:N} — "nothing to commit" — which is benign there
(everything IS upstream) but indistinguishable from the stranded case at the API. A follow-up
row could distinguish "already uploaded" vs "stranded" (e.g. compare local vs pushed SHAs before
the early return); the P2 fix here is the stranded case.

FIX DIRECTION (foreman owns): make the push part of the atomicity boundary — on push failure,
roll back the local commit (git reset --hard HEAD~1 in the export clone, files are re-rendered
next attempt) so the next export re-renders + re-pushes; and/or in stageAndCommit's early-return
path, check whether the local HEAD is already pushed (git cherry / rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD)
and if not, push it (recovering the stranded commit) with the real SHA in the response. Include a
regression test: push fails -> re-export same ids -> target must receive the files.
Acceptance: after a failed-push export, the retry (same ids, push now possible) MUST result in the
answers present upstream AND commit_sha non-empty in the response.
"
}

title: [P3] TestApplyMemLimitMB_RoundTrip hardcodes a 4096 MiB probe and fails EPERM under any lower ambient RLIMIT_AS cap — the exact shape the memcap wrapper targets (QA chaos-resource cell red on a capped host; reproduced locally under ulimit -v 3145728)

DOGFOOD 2026-10-16 (run 18), phase 2 — the fleet's fresh-system QA battery (bunker-qa.sh; agent
913faf73 on bunker-mvp; tested HEAD 31f49319) graded its `chaos-resource` cell rc=1, and the failure
reproduces on the control host with the exact same string.

QA CELL EVIDENCE (bunker-qa evidence jsonl, cell chaos-resource):
  rc=1 under cap (cap=3145728KB child_saw=3145728 subshell_saw=3145728 parent_saw=unlimited):
    --- FAIL: TestApplyMemLimitMB_RoundTrip (0.07s) FAIL FAIL
        github.com/totalwindupflightsystems/off-by-one/internal/sandbox 1.848s
    --- FAIL: TestChat_PeriodicStatusUntilAgentFrame (5.36s) FAIL

LOCAL DISCRIMINATING PROBE (control arm first, then the same 3 GiB AS cap the cell used):
  $ go test ./internal/sandbox/ -run TestApplyMemLimitMB_RoundTrip -count=1
    ok  github.com/totalwindupflightsystems/off-by-one/internal/sandbox  0.004s
  $ bash -c 'ulimit -v 3145728; go test ./internal/sandbox/ -run TestApplyMemLimitMB_RoundTrip -count=1'
    --- FAIL: TestApplyMemLimitMB_RoundTrip (0.00s)
        memcap_test.go:190: roundtrip helper failed: exit status 1
            ApplyMemLimitMB(4096): sandbox: setrlimit RLIMIT_AS=4096 MiB: operation not permitted
    FAIL  (rc=1)

CAUSE: the test's helper child asks for RLIMIT_AS = 4096 MiB while the process tree already carries a
3072 MiB hard cap. setrlimit above an inherited hard limit returns EPERM, so the round-trip assertion
fails for an ENVIRONMENT reason, not a product reason — nothing in the memcap wrapper is wrong here.

WHY IT STILL DESERVES A ROW: the deployment shapes this project targets are exactly the ones that
carry an ambient AS cap — containers, CI runners, and the fleet's own fresh-system QA battery (the
Hermes terminal sandbox also caps at 4 GiB, where the 4096 MiB probe sits exactly ON the boundary).
Anyone running the documented `go test ./...` inside one of them gets a red suite and has to read the
helper to learn it is not their code; today that cost the QA battery a whole cell and this run a probe
cycle.

FIX DIRECTION: derive the probe from the ambient hard limit (syscall.Getrlimit(RLIMIT_AS)) and skip
with a reason when it is below the probe — e.g. t.Skipf("ambient RLIMIT_AS hard cap %d MiB < probe
4096 MiB") — or probe below the ambient cap. Acceptance: the package suite passes both bare and under
`ulimit -v 3145728`, and the QA chaos-resource cell grades green on a capped host.

(Separately: the same battery's `ci-act` cell exited rc=1 with a truncated act log — the harness's own
rule is that "a failed act leg is never graded OK; hosted CI is authoritative", and the full log lived
on the now-destroyed agent, so this run deliberately files NO row on it — it is unattributed, and the
QA lane owns that cell.)

title: [P3] check-binary-fresh fails a Makefile-only change: 'Makefile' is in the code-path filter, so any Makefile edit forces the byte comparison, where a rebuilt binary can never match the deployed one (the embedded version stamp alone differs) - a rebuild+service restart is demanded for a change that cannot alter compiled code
foreman_note: Observed tick 441: merging the OB-DIST-003 change (Makefile gained deploy-distribute / check-distribute-deploy / check-distribute-deploy-selftest) made 'make check-binary-fresh' exit 1 with './off-by-one is stale - source changed since it was built' although no Go file changed. Mechanism: Makefile line ~66 diffs only 'cmd/ internal/ web/ sql/ pkg/ go.mod go.sum Makefile' against the stamped revision; a Makefile hit makes that diff non-empty, so the target falls through to the fresh-build byte comparison, and a rebuild differs from the deployed artifact by the embedded version stamp alone - the comparison can never pass without a rebuild. The tick's own deploy closed it (make build at 69472a2a, kill MainPID 7083 -> 2852325, check-binary-fresh PASS, gate-deploy PASS, endpoints 7/7, stats intact), but the false positive will recur on every Makefile touch and it also makes the 'code paths unchanged' tolerance useless for Makefile edits. Candidate fixes: drop Makefile from the diff filter and rely on the Go paths + go.mod/go.sum (a Makefile edit only changes the compiled result through LDFLAGS/ldflags, which the stamp already reflects), or compare the resolved stamp instead of the bytes when the only diff is the Makefile. Acceptance: 'make check-binary-fresh' exits 0 on a tree whose only difference from the stamped revision is the Makefile, while still exiting 1 when Go source differs, with a regression test covering both arms.
worker_summary: Foreman-direct: dropped Makefile from code-path filter in three locations — Makefile:66 (check-binary-fresh), scripts/check-deploy:63 (resolve-stamp leg), scripts/check-deploy-test.sh:97 (dirty-code-path detection). All three now use: cmd/ internal/ web/ sql/ pkg/ go.mod go.sum (no Makefile). Verified: Makefile-only edit → exit 0 (up to date); Go source change → exit 1/2 (stale). Judge PASS verdict 71a8db00. CI green on all commits.

title: [P2] RECURRENCE of DF-37 (answer-corpus arm) — the dedup 409 still returns submission_id:"" when the hit is a VERIFIED ANSWER rather than a queue entry, so the documented "poll the existing submission" contract is unsatisfiable on that arm
reasoning:
DOGFOOD 2026-10-20 (run 19) — scratch instance built from HEAD fda8b3a2, seeded 2785 classes.

REPRO (verbatim; the tuple must match the corpus answer stored env=docker/lang=go/version=latest):
  $ curl -s -X POST :18801/api/v1/problems/submit -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"problem_class":"go-http-validation-auth-input","environment":"docker","language":"go",
           "version":"latest","cadence":"post-debug","description":"dup arm"}'
    HTTP 409
    {"submission_id":"","problem_class":"go-http-validation-auth-input","status":"deduplicated",
     "position":0,"estimated_time":"","existing_solutions":1,"related_problems":[...7 ids...],
     "resolved_tools":[],"missing_tools":[]}
  Repeat -> byte-identical: submission_id is "" on both, so the second call could not even point at the first.

DOCS PROMISE (quoted verbatim):
  README.md:217-220 — "A submission is deduplicated against the queue and the verified-answer corpus ...
    409 with "status": "deduplicated" and the existing submission_id (the same id the first submit returned)"
  docs/api-reference.md:73 — "When that tuple is already queued/in progress or already has a verified answer,
    no second job is created: the response carries status deduplicated and the EXISTING submission_id ...
    with its queue position"
  The queue-entry arm DOES satisfy it (verified in-browser this run: second SPA submit of the same tuple →
  409 {"submission_id":"sub_fd245d","status":"deduplicated","position":1}), which is precisely what DF-37's
  2026-10-13 fix covered.

WHY THE ARM CANNOT BE SATISFIED AS WRITTEN: internal/api/handlers.go:340-355 stamps the existing queue
entry's id when ErrDuplicate comes from findPendingDuplicate (queue.go:254-261); the corpus-answer arm
returns ErrDuplicate with NO entry (queue.go:266-272), so there is no id to stamp. The response carries
existing_solutions:1 but no pointer to the answer and no next-step hint — a scripted Muster consumer that
follows the docs is left with an id that resolves to nothing (GET /api/v1/queue/ → 404/empty).
fix_direction:
Pick one and make it explicit on the wire:
(a) carry a resolvable pointer for the answered arm — e.g. answer_id/class + a discover hint (found/answer),
    or a synthesized stable id that GET /api/v1/queue/{id} resolves; or
(b) document the answered arm in README + docs/api-reference ("submission_id: "" + existing_solutions > 0
    = already answered, call POST /api/v1/problems/discover"), and add a distinguishing field
    (reason: "queued" | "answered") so the two 409 arms are not byte-identical.
Acceptance: a scripted consumer can act on either dedup arm without reading the source; a regression test
covers the CORPUS arm (the existing test covers only the queue arm).

title: [P2] The Submit form's fixed environment vocabulary (Any/dev/staging/prod/ci/local) cannot express the values the corpus and its own docs use (docker, linux), so the documented "already has a verified answer → 409" dedup is unreachable from the SPA: a UI user re-queues a solve of an answered class while the panel says "1 existing solution found."
reasoning:
DOGFOOD 2026-10-20 (run 19) — driven in a real browser against a HEAD instance seeded with the bundled
corpus (2785 classes / 2883 answers), with window.fetch instrumented to capture the wire bodies.

EVIDENCE:
  Explore (same build): drilling the class go-http-validation-auth-input renders
    class -> env "docker" -> lang "go" -> version "latest" -> answer (VERIFIED, detail pane 4285 chars).
  Submit form: document.querySelectorAll('#submit-env option') ->
    '', 'dev', 'staging', 'prod', 'ci', 'local'      (no docker, no linux)
    version is free text; language offers go/python/rust/typescript/javascript/java/c/cpp.
  UI submit #1 (class above, env=local, lang=go, version empty) ->
    HTTP 200 {"submission_id":"sub_fd245d","status":"queued","position":3,"estimated_time":"1m30s",
              "existing_solutions":1,...}
    panel: "QUEUED ... Queue position: #3 ... 1 existing solution found." -> a NEW solve is queued for a
    class that already holds a verified answer served by discover in 0.68 ms.
  UI submit #2 (identical tuple) -> HTTP 409 dedup, panel "DEDUPLICATED ... Already queued (sub_fd245d),
    position 1 — this problem was already solved or is already in the queue." (DF-43's fix holds.)
  Docs/API use env values the form cannot express: README's submit example uses "environment": "linux";
  the corpus answers store env=docker/lang=go/version=latest — so the form's tuple can never equal the
  corpus tuple, and the corpus arm of the documented dedup is unreachable from the product's own UI.

IMPACT: the SPA is the human entry point of a system whose stated economics are "convert idle compute
cycles". A user is told an answer already exists and the lab still spends a solve re-answering it; the
resulting confusion ("why did dedup not fire?") lands on the user, not the docs.
fix_direction:
Make the environment input able to express reality: free-text with a datalist seeded from the taxonomy's
actual env values (docker/linux/... appear there), or at minimum add the observed vocabulary. Optionally
also dedup by class when existing_solutions > 0 and hand back the answer pointer (discover link) instead of
queueing a duplicate solve. Acceptance: submitting an already-answered class from the UI reaches the
409/answered path, or the form can express the corpus/docs tuple.

MECHANISM: when core.hooksPath is set, git looks for hooks ONLY there — $GIT_DIR/hooks is ignored. So the

ids / dangling depends_on (the tick contract calls a duplicate id a board-lint ERROR that blocks EVERY
commit in the repo) is therefore inert exactly where it is advertised as installed.

IMPACT: a duplicate-id or dangling-dep commit from any lane writing this board sails through; the failure
surfaces later as a repo-wide commit block or as a silently unreachable row. Nothing reports the gap —
`boardctl validate` is a manual/CI invocation, not a commit gate, and the effective hook prints nothing
about the board.

NOTE (not a claim about boardctl's intent): the global hook is a fleet-wide install, so the same
override applies to every repo in the fleet that boardctl installed into.
fix_direction:
Fix lives in boardctl's install path (cross-project: this board only records it).
`boardctl install` must write the board-lint block into the EFFECTIVE hook path — resolve it with

repo's own hooks from there) — and must detect the override at install time and either adapt or fail with a
named remedy instead of reporting a successful install. Acceptance: in a repo whose core.hooksPath is set
globally, a commit that introduces a duplicate task id (or a dangling depends_on) is still BLOCKED, or the
